title: Bushwick meeting addresses federal funding cuts and increased ICE raids - NewsBreak
text: BUSHWICK, Brooklyn (PIX 11) — Community members and lawmakers came together for a town hall in Bushwick Wednesday, calling on the state to step up protections for vulnerable residents at risk of losing healthcare and vital services — as well as tackling growing concerns about ICE enforcement. The meeting follows the passage of the Trump administration’s “One Big Beautiful Bill,” which became law earlier this month. Immigration advocates with the organization Make the Road New York said the sweeping federal legislation could result in more than a million New Yorkers losing access to healthcare coverage and other essential services. “That’s going to affect a lot of our community members that are at risk of losing a lot of essential services — Medicare, SNAP,” said Jennifer Hernandez of Make the Road New York. “We’re here to collaborate and to ask elected [officials] what we can do as a state to fight back.” Organizers are also raising the alarm over ICE enforcement efforts targeting immigrant communities. Maria, who’s originally from Mexico and has lived in the U.S. for more than 20 years, lives in constant fear of being separated from her family due to ICE enforcement. She said it’s changed the way she moves through daily life. “My children love going to museums but, for example, we’re not doing that at the moment just out of precaution for them and for all of our family,” Maria said. She’s one of several community members who shared personal stories to highlight the urgent need for lawmakers to hold a special legislative session in Albany. Attendees and organizers are calling on state officials to fill gaps to mitigate budget cuts and ensure New Yorkers have access to vital services, such as healthcare coverage and nutrition programs. The community is also demanding a ban on local law enforcement from cooperating with ICE agents. Despite her fears, Maria is vowing to continue speaking out. “Of course we’re scared, but we also have to stand up and face things, especially because of our children,” she said. The community is pushing for the passage of the New York for All Act — a bill aimed at protecting immigrant communities by limiting cooperation between local law enforcement and ICE agents. PIX 11 News reached out to Governor Kathy Hochul’s office to ask whether she plans to call a special legislative session and are still waiting to hear back. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to PIX11.
